what: LPL Financial is the largest independent broker-dealer in the United States. Financial advisers who want to run their own practices affiliate with it, and LPL provides the custody, technology, compliance and research behind them.
customers: More than 32,000 financial advisers and about 1,200 financial institutions, and through them individual investors.
money: fees and commissions on client assets
interest earned on client cash balances
platform and technology charges to affiliated advisers
moat: A platform advisers build their businesses on, where moving means re-papering every client account, plus scale that lets it offer services no small firm can.
risks: Falling interest rates reduce income earned on client cash
Debt of about $8 billion from acquisitions
Adviser recruitment costs rise when competition for them increases
Regulatory scrutiny of cash sweep programmes has increased across the industry
opportunities: Revenue grew about 37% last year and about 25% a year over three years
Analysts see about 47% upside from current levels
It keeps winning advisers from wirehouses and smaller competitors
watch: Net new assets and adviser headcount growth.
